finding.text: The class card titles can't be read. On every dark class card (View, Page, Router, App, Sidebar, Shell…) the name is dark grey text on the dark ground, so the main word on the card is close to invisible (colour 1, content: the card's name is its point). Evidence: shots/127-0-0-1-60161-framework/3440.png, Core band; 400.png, last band. The `.page-link` inside `page-surface-dark` needs the light link colour.

Requirement 5 ("find any hard-coded copies and remove them") is not met. `ext/Mention/maps/refs.js` still holds a hand-typed `icon` for every name. `sync.mjs` only re-copies them when someone remembers to run it, so changing a page's icon does not update its mentions until then. Evidence: diff, refs.js lines 27–61.

`/framework/old/` shows two sidebars at 1200 and wider. The old `render()` builds its own Sidebar rooted at a page with no children, so a second, empty column titled "Framework (old)" sits beside the real one. Evidence: shots/127-0-0-1-60161-framework-old/sheet.png, 1200/1920/3440 (left band). layout.json reports empty 0.687 at 1200 and 0.82 at 3440.

Requirement 3 ("every class gets an icon") isn't shown. The diff adds no `icon:` to any page. Every card visible in the shots has an icon, but no list of the class pages that were checked was left behind.

The dark mention colours `#17161a` / `#e8e8ea` are typed into Mention.js instead of read from tokens (code/css). The file's own comment admits they repeat Page.css. If the dark surface is ever retuned, the two will drift apart.

The UX section draws live thumbnails (Sign in, Wizard, Tree) where the other sections draw icon items. That comes from UX's own `previews()`, so it is not new. Still, it breaks the "icon, name, one line" grid that requirement 2 describes. Evidence: framework/3440.png, right column.
On the sprawl demo page at 1920, the paragraphs run 1201px wide (layout.json widest_text 1201). That is well past a readable measure, because a section's text gets the whole 60rem column.

Requirement 7: nothing in the diff or task folder shows that @task-mastermind-panel2-sessions was told about sprawl. Sprawl also went beyond the "plain grid" the brief asked for (it adds a JS balancing pass). That is reasonable, and it is recorded in design/layout, but it overlaps work the brief assigned to Panel 2.

The dark class cards' titles and icons are unreadable: dark grey on a near-black ground (View, Page, Router, App, Sidebar, Shell, Item, List) at every width. The `.page-preview.page-surface-dark .page-preview-title` fix in Page.css is not winning (colour 1; ask 4) — shots/framework/1200.png, Core band; same in 400.png and 3440.png.

/framework/old/ still draws two sidebars: two "Framework" brands side by side at 1200 and up, two stacked headers at 400 (ask 1; page structure) — shots/framework-old/sheet.png; layout.json shows two `mode-btn` wraps at 1200/1920/3440.

No class page got a new icon. The diff adds icons only to ext/sprawl and /framework/old, and ask 3 asks for an audit of every class page. Every card visible in the shots has an icon, but only the first screen of each section was shot, so this is unproven — shots/framework/3440.png.

Some sections are not "icon, name, one-line description" (ask 2). UX shows live thumbnails instead, and UI, which has its own sidebar heading, has no section (it has no children, so `wall_rungs()` skips it) — shots/framework/3440.png, UX column; sidebar vs. sections.

Icons are not from one source yet (ask 5). `maps/refs.js` still hard-codes every icon as a cache; `live()` only overrides it when the page has already been loaded this session. This is acceptable as a fallback, but the hard-coded copies were not removed.

Sprawl became a new module, `ext/sprawl`, with a JS balancing pass, where the brief asked for a plain grid plus a one-line name in design/layout. The JS pass works (three columns at 3440, one stacked column at 1200), but Panel 2 owns that later (ask 7). The design/layout entry is a 70-word line, not one line.
At 1920 the sprawl demo's paragraphs run 1201px wide, so the `.measure.start` fix is not visible in the shot — layout.json widest_text 1201 at 1920.
At 400 the five stat tiles push Core down to 730px, so only one card shows above the fold — shots/framework/400.png.

Ask 5 says "find any hard-coded copies [of icons] and remove them". `ext/Mention/maps/refs.js` still holds a hand-written `icon:` for every entry. It is now a cache with a live lookup in front of it, so a page that hasn't been built this session still shows the old icon until someone runs `sync.mjs`. Breadcrumbs were not checked at all (diff: Mention.js `live()`, refs.js, sync.mjs).

`ext/Mention/sync.mjs` defaults to `http://framework-home.localhost`, this task's own worktree server, which stops existing once the branch merges. Run with no argument after merge, the second pass fails to load every page and changes nothing. Default it to the site's own host, `monorepo.localhost` (diff: sync.mjs, `base_url`).

There is no evidence that ask 3 ("every class gets an icon") was checked. The diff adds no `icon:` to any page. Every card visible in the shots has an icon (`shots/…-framework/1200.png`, Core), but the shots only cover the first screen.

Every card cuts its one-line description off with "…" at every width ("Everything between a url changing and the DOM…", `1200.png`, Core row 1). The owner asked for the description, and a cut-off sentence doesn't give it.

At 1920 the Core grid runs six cards across, each about 230px (~14rem), which is under the brief's `minmax(min(100%, 16rem), 1fr)`. The new page reuses the existing `previews()` grid instead of the 16rem one (`sheet.png`, 1920).
The UX section renders screenshot thumbnails (Sign in, Wizard, Tree), not the icon + name + description items asked for in ask 2 (`3440.png`, right column).

Ask 6 asked for sprawl to be named "in one line" on the layout page. The readme entry in `design/layout/readme.md` is a 70-word paragraph. The Sprawl demo's opening paragraph is also dense with CSS (`shots/…-ext-sprawl/400.png`, band 2 takes 25% of the screen).

Ask 7 said to use a plain grid. Instead the task built a new JS balancing module, `ext/sprawl`. Its header cites an owner follow-up correction asking for this, so it is accepted, but the requirements file doesn't record that correction.

The new /framework/ skips every sidebar section that has no children of its own, so **UI**, which the brief names in its section list, has no section. Neither do Start here, AI, AI 2, Research, FAQ, Versus, Audit and Sandbox (requirement 2; layout 8). Evidence: shots/…-framework/3440.png, top band, runs Core → Styles → UX, while the sidebar beside it lists UI between Styles and UX with no expand arrow. `wall_rungs()` drops `!page.children.size`. The owner said "I want to see all the things in the framework." A section with no children should still get a card, for example in a "Pages" section placed first.

Card descriptions are cut off with "…" even at 3440, where there is room to spare. For example, "A chainable wrapper over a DOM element, with…" (wrapping 24). Evidence: shots/…-framework/3440.png, Core cards. A two-line clamp on a 1000px column hides the one line the owner asked each card to show.
At 3440 the top half of the screen holds a 600px hero and five stat tiles, with about 2,500px of empty width beside them (layout 7). layout.json: empty 0.62 at 3440. The wall starts at roughly y=560.

Inside each section, the cards come from the existing `previews()` grid, not the brief's `minmax(min(100%, 16rem), 1fr)`. At 1920 that gives about 6 cards of ~15rem per row. It is close enough, but it is not the number the brief asked for. Evidence: shots/…-framework/1920.png, Core row.

"Icons from one source" (requirement 5) is only partly live. A page that has not loaded this session still gets its icon from the `refs.js` cache, which stays out of date until someone runs `sync.mjs` by hand. Breadcrumbs were never checked. The trade-off is written down in Mention.js.

"Framework (old)" is now the last entry in the main sidebar, so a backup sits in everyone's navigation. Evidence: shots/…-framework/3440.png, the bottom of the sidebar. Linking to it only from the page footer would be enough.

Icons still come from two places (requirement 5). `ext/Mention/maps/refs.js` keeps a hand-typed `icon` for all 34 names. It is used whenever the page isn't loaded yet ("cold case"), and `sync.mjs` has to be re-run by hand to keep it right. The brief said "find any hard-coded copies and remove them". Either build the map from the page tree, or tell the owner plainly that the copy is kept.

The UX section breaks the "icon, name and description" card (requirement 2). At 3440 its cards are screenshots with only a name (Auth, Wizard, Tree, Menu) and no description, because `preview_card()` drops the description whenever a thumbnail is present. Every other section shows icon + name + description — shots/framework/3440.png, right column.

UI is in the sidebar but has no section on the page (requirement 2: "one section per sidebar section"). `wall_rungs()` skips any section with no child pages, so UI, Audit and Sandbox are missing — sidebar vs page body at shots/framework/3440.png.

The brief said to use a plain grid and leave adaptive column heights to Panel 2 (requirement 7). Instead the build added a new module, `ext/sprawl`, that measures each section with JS and balances the columns. It works and it never moves a section while you read, but it is a second, early answer to the question Panel 2 owns. Tell @task-mastermind-panel2-sessions about it.
Card descriptions are cut off with "…" at every width ("Everything between a url changing and the DOM…", "resizable by its own edge. Not…") — shots/framework/1200.png, Core band (wrapping 24).
At 400, the five stat tiles end on a lone "Config files" tile (layout 11) — shots/framework/400.png, band 3.

On the sprawl demo at 1920 there is room for only one 60rem column. Each section card stretches about 1530px wide while its text is held to the reading width, leaving a large blank right half (layout 10) — shots/framework-ext-sprawl/1920.png.

Icons don't all come from one place yet (requirement 5). `ext/Mention/maps/refs.js` still keeps its own copy of each icon, and that copy is only refreshed when someone re-runs `sync.mjs`. The new `live()` lookup reads the real page only if that page has already loaded in this session. So if you change a page's icon, a mention of a page nobody has opened yet still shows the old icon. The requirement's own test, "change one page's icon and every surface updates", fails. Evidence: diff, Mention.js `live()` comment ("cold case: … cache stands").

Requirement 7 said "use plain grid here", and that adaptive column heights belong to Panel 2 later. Instead the build adds a new module, `ext/sprawl`, with a JavaScript column balancer (a ResizeObserver, sections measured off-screen, then placed into whichever column is shortest). That is the adaptive-height system the owner called "a big question", now built a second way next to Panel 2 (law 6). The diff shows no note to @task-mastermind-panel2-sessions. Either fall back to plain `auto-fit` grid flow, or hand the balancer to Panel 2 and record that decision.

`sprawl()` returns an empty grid and fills it only on its first ResizeObserver callback. A tab opened in the background shows no sections until it is focused. The off-screen measuring box sits on `<body>`, outside the page's own styles, so the measured heights can differ from the real ones. The observer is never disconnected.

The module grid inside each section uses the existing `.page-previews` width of `--column: 14em`, not the `16rem` the brief asked for (requirement 6). The result is close at every width (shots/…-framework/1200.png: three cards across), but it is not the number the brief wrote.

Every card description stops at two lines with an ellipsis, even at 3440 where there is room: "Everything between a url changing and the DOM…" (shots/…-framework/3440.png, the Core band). The brief asked for the one-line description, and here it is cut off mid-sentence.
At 3440, the first column holds AI and UI, one small card each. That leaves a 60rem column almost empty next to the full Core and Styles columns (shots/…-framework/3440.png, sections band).

At 400, the title and five stat tiles fill the first screen. Only one card shows above the fold (shots/…-framework/400.png). The intro sentence also tells the reader what is coming ("Everything below is the framework itself… click any card to open it") instead of letting the cards show it (content: show, don't tell).
`ext/sprawl` has `readme.md` and `page.js` but no `doc/` folder. Every module is meant to have all three.

ext/filesystem (the FsFile class, which the brief names by hand as a class) still draws as a LIGHT card on /framework/ext/, while Doc, Tabs and Saver draw dark (requirement 4). Evidence: shots/…-framework-ext/1920.png, row 1, the "File system" card. `Doc.is_class(this.subject)` sees the module's namespace, not the FsFile class inside it.

The icon check (requirement 3) covered only the 27 page-backed entries in refs.js, not every class module the sidebar sections name. ext/Inbox, which the brief names, is not checked anywhere, and it is not even a child of ext/. Evidence: the minion's task.jsonl log, "Review note 4".

At 3440, the AI and UI sections each hold one ~390px card alone in a ~960px column (layout 10). Evidence: shots/…-framework/3440.png, left column. This is the cost of giving every leaf section its own section; it is acceptable, but worth knowing.

The five stat tiles sit between the title and the module grid, so the core concepts are not the first thing under the title (page 2). Evidence: shots/…-framework/400.png, where the first module card sits at y≈700.
The intro paragraph on /framework/ext/sprawl/ runs about 85 words (content 3). Evidence: shots/…-framework-ext-sprawl/3440.png, band 2.
The section headings (Core, Styles, …) name their topic but carry no one-line gist (page 11). Evidence: shots/…-framework/1920.png.

Icons are not yet read from one source (requirement 5): `ext/Mention/maps/refs.js` still hard-codes 35 `icon:` values (and now `class_card:` flags too). `live()` replaces them only for pages already loaded in this session, so a mention of a page nobody has opened yet still shows the old copied icon. The brief says "find any hard-coded copies and remove them" — diff, `refs.js` lines 27–64.

On `/framework/` at 3440, the first column holds AI and UI as one-card sections inside a 60rem track: a 16rem card with about 40rem of grey beside it, under a heading that repeats the card's own name ("AI" over "AI"). It is balanced by height, as asked, but the top band reads as dead space — shots/…-framework/3440.png, left column.

The dark class look reuses `page-surface-dark` and adds no new `.class-card` word. That is right by law 6 (one of everything), but the brief's "one CSS word" now has a name that doesn't say "class". Record the name chosen in `ext/Mention`'s or `core/Page`'s doc so the next agent finds it.

`/framework/old/` shows two titles in a row: "Framework (old)" and then the old h1 — shots/…-framework-old/1200.png, top band. Its 3440 clock band is 86% empty, but this page is the untouched backup, so that is accepted.

Requirement 3 (every class gets an icon) has no audit recorded in the task. A grep finds only `ext/Doc/overview/urls/page.js` among `new Doc(` pages with no `icon:`, and that is a sub-page, not a class. No blank icon shows in any shot.
At 1920 the hero and the stats tiles take about 43% of the first screen, so only the AI and Core sections are above the fold — shots/…-framework/1920.png, bands 1–2.

answer.reply: declined: this is the architectural cold-case limit (requirement 5's own live() lookup already covers every page loaded this session). Confirmed by reading core/Page's declare()/source_children() directly: a string-declared child's map entry stays null until something actually visits it, so there is no synchronous page-tree Mention could read an unvisited page's icon from without an eager-load-every-page-at-boot change, which is a sitewide architecture change against the framework's own documented lazy-load design and far outside this task's fence. The two-tier answer (live lookup first, sync.mjs-regenerated refs.js cache as fallback, now defaulting to the real site host) is this task's final answer. Raised and declined with the same reasoning across review rounds 2, 3, 4 and 5; closing it here.

reply.text: The decline traces the actual limit in `core/Page`'s `declare()`/`source_children()` — an unvisited page's map entry stays null, so there is no page-tree Mention could read from without an eager-load-every-page change, and that's a sitewide architecture shift outside this task's fence. The live-lookup-plus-regenerated-cache fallback is a reasonable two-tier answer, and the same reasoning held across four review rounds without a counter-argument appearing.

answer.reply: noted: a one-card leaf section (AI, UI) in a 60rem column beside full sections is the cost of greedy balancing with very uneven section sizes - the report's own words call this 'balanced by height, as asked'. Not changing the balancer for one visual edge case.

noted: page-surface-dark is the existing dark-surface word (core/Page/words.js), reused rather than inventing `.class-card` per CLAUDE.md law 6. ext/Mention's readme.md already documents the choice and the specificity trap in full; adding another doc pointer would duplicate it.
noted: /framework/old/ is the untouched backup of the original page, kept verbatim on purpose (deliverable 1) - the reviewer's own text calls the empty clock band 'accepted' for that reason.

noted: checked by hand in review round 5 - core/Page, core/Item, core/List and ext/filesystem's FsFile all already had icon+subject set; zero blank icons found in any shot across all six rounds. Logged in task.jsonl rather than a separate audit file.
noted: the stats-tiles-before-the-module-grid order is carried over from the page this task started from, not something this task changed.
